claims.text: Conventional automotive exhaust catalysts synthesized by traditional methods use high PGM loadings.

A closed-loop platform integrating automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated ageing, activity screening, machine learning, and Bayesian optimisation will produce catalysts with superior catalytic activity.
The closed-loop platform will produce catalysts with superior durability.
The closed-loop platform will reduce PGM consumption relative to conventional catalyst synthesis.
Systematic exploration of multielement formulations can lower PGM loading while improving nanoscale active-site distribution and stability.
Optimized nanostructural heterogeneity enhances catalytic-site efficiency and durability.
Synergistic interactions between non-noble and noble-metal sites enhance catalytic-site efficiency and durability.
Machine learning and Bayesian optimisation can guide synthesis toward compositions with enhanced active-site distribution.
Machine learning and Bayesian optimisation can guide synthesis toward compositions with improved thermal stability.
Improved active-site distribution, thermal stability, and non-noble/noble-metal synergy allow catalysts to retain high activity with reduced PGM content.
Improved active-site distribution, thermal stability, and non-noble/noble-metal synergy allow catalysts to retain durability with reduced PGM content.
Closed-loop-optimized catalysts will improve catalytic activity by at least 10–20% relative to conventional catalysts.
Closed-loop-optimized catalysts will have enhanced durability relative to conventional catalysts.
Closed-loop-optimized catalysts will use less PGM than conventional catalysts.
The proposed comparison should use identical simulated exhaust and accelerated thermal-ageing conditions for optimized and conventional catalysts.
Laboratory results from automated solvothermal synthesis may not extrapolate to industrial production or long-term field performance without additional validation.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome quantifies only catalytic activity as a 10–20% improvement and describes durability merely as enhanced, whereas the falsification rule appears to require a 10–20% improvement in both activity and durability.
